native_result.query: In which century do Diversity in Pottery Decoration and Diversity in Pottery Form show opposite growth trends for the first time, with Pottery Decoration increasing significantly and Pottery Form declining simultaneously?
native_result.HypoA: In 1700 BCE, for the first time, Diversity in Pottery Decoration shows a significant increase while Diversity in Pottery Form experiences a notable decline. This marks a unique divergence in the growth trends of these two cultural capital variables.
native_result.HypoB: The first century in which Pottery Decoration diversity rises significantly (+1.45 Z, from -0.48 to +0.97) while Pottery Form diversity declines simultaneously (-1.87 Z, from +0.74 to -1.13) is the 18th century BCE, i.e., 1800-1700 BCE - the unique opposite-trend bin across the whole 4300-500 BCE record.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load capital.csv with comma-decimal parsing (decimal=','); confirm 39 century anchors at BCE 4300->500 (100-yr steps, no missing). 2) Map variables: ZKeform = Diversity in Pottery Form, Zkeverz = Diversity in Pottery Decoration (both Cultural Capital per study context); verify exact agreement (37/37 overlapping anchors) with raw PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration in time_series_data.csv. 3) Compute growth trend as chronological first difference between consecutive 100-yr bins. 4) Select bins where dForm<0 AND dDec>0 (simultaneous opposite trends). 5) Take the earliest qualifying bin in absolute time = first occurrence = 1800->1700 BCE. 6) Label the century as 18th century BCE (span 1800-1700 BCE). 7) Robustness: repeat with magnitude thresholds 0.0-1.2 Z (unchanged); cross-check the interpolated 1-yr series signs (identical); document the +0.0015 anchor-boundary interpolation artifact.
